beats.narration_en: At night, these lane lines seem to glow, lit by nothing but your own headlights.
Zoom in, and the paint is packed with thousands of tiny glass beads.
Light enters a bead, bends, bounces off the back, and bends again, straight back toward where it came from.
Without those beads, the same white paint looks dull and almost disappears in the dark.
That extra glow can buy a driver a crucial extra second to see the lane at night.
A tiny glass sphere, doing a precise job, on every striped road in the country.
